clue.text: I'd reordered fruit juice packaged to go

indicators.note: packaged means the juice is bundled up together with the fruit, the two sitting side by side
the two letters of I'd are put into a new order, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A shopper reorders a packet of fruit juice to take away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reordered' turns I'D into DI. 'to go' looks like takeaway language, but 'go' is the definition, with 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish from sight is to go away, so going and vanishing are synonyms.

clue.text: Make local a gift

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
a native is a local of a place

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn a present into something homely.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a gift or donation, especially an official one.

clue.text: Take one away from this to make it divisible by two

definitions.text: Take one away from this to make it divisible by two

parts.words: Take one away from this to make it divisible by two
parts.note: works two ways: subtract 1 from the number and the result divides by 2; remove one letter from the word and what is left means divisible by two

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle about a number that becomes even when one is subtracted.
explanation.walkthrough: Subtracting 1 gives six; dropping the first letter of the number word leaves EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the odd number one more than six, so taking one away leaves an even total.

clue.text: Friendly fool sound asleep here, perhaps

indicators.note: sound tells us that the words are said aloud to make the answer

parts.note: pally is friendly and an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A good-natured idiot fast asleep in this spot, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks part of 'sound asleep', but it signals that 'pally ass' is spoken. The definition 'asleep here, perhaps' describes a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a straw-filled mattress, the kind of thing a person might sleep on.

clue.text: English author including page for sculptor

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the page goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Gertrude Stein was an American author

explanation.surface: A writer from England takes on a page about an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a leading twentieth-century sculptor working in Britain.

clue.text: Enthusiast taken up by staff on a building like the Millennium Dome?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed below, so the A comes after
by means held by, so the reversed piece sits within the staff

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means lifted upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fanatic

explanation.surface: A fan is carried aloft on a pole to a dome-shaped building in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses the enthusiast because this is a down clue. The Millennium Dome is the huge round tent-like building in Greenwich, London, now called The O2.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually domed, which describes the Dome; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Cover case before dispatching a dozen in box

definitions.text: Cover case before dispatching a dozen in box

parts.words: Cover case before dispatching a dozen in box
parts.note: read as a courtroom: the judge reviews the whole case before sending out the twelve jurors who sit in the jury box

explanation.surface: Someone packs a case before shipping twelve items in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about packing and posting; the real picture is a trial judge's closing review of the evidence before the jury of twelve retires.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's closing summary of the evidence covers the whole case before the jury retires.

clue.text: Skin problems upset this dry old stick

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: warts are small growths, a skin problem

explanation.surface: A grumpy old person whose skin problems upset them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns WARTS round. 'dry old stick' looks like a dull elderly person but literally means a dried stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is the dried stalk of cereal plants, a dry stick of a kind.

clue.text: 6 lions destroyed one dictator in Rome

parts.note: the answer to 6 across, read as an instruction in a down light, says to write a total going upwards: a total is a sum

indicators.note: destroyed means smashed up, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lions savaged a tyrant in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 6 across, a phrasal verb meaning summarise; read in this down light it says write SUM upwards, giving MUS. 'destroyed' rearranges LIONS and I into SOLINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was the Fascist dictator who ruled Italy from Rome.

clue.text: A particularly nice scholar takes favourite boy inside

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so the favourite holds the boy
inside confirms the boy is placed within the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A fussy academic brings in their favourite lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' here is the old sense, precise or finicky, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means finely precise, so an overly precise scholar is a stickler for detail.

clue.text: All that's left of early maternal attachment

definitions.text: All that's left of early maternal attachment

parts.words: All that's left of early maternal attachment
parts.note: the umbilical cord once attached a baby to its mother; the small scar it leaves on the belly is all that remains

explanation.surface: A wistful note about how little remains of a childhood bond with one's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attachment' sounds emotional, but it is the physical cord joining a foetus to its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is the scar where the umbilical cord was once attached.

clue.text: Disaster -I crashed, having taken off

indicators.note: crashed suggests something smashed up, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot reports a disaster: having taken off, they crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' sounds like an aircraft leaving the ground, but it means mimicked or mocked. 'crashed' rearranges DISASTER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic and mock them, which is what a satirist does.

clue.text: The sort of annuity one inevitably benefits from?

definitions.text: The sort of annuity one inevitably benefits from?

parts.words: The sort of annuity one inevitably benefits from?
parts.note: read 'one' as a single person: in this scheme members pool money and the last survivor collects everything, so in the end just one person profits

explanation.surface: A question about a pension that is guaranteed to pay out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like the general 'you', but it means a single person: the scheme pays its income to the survivors until only one is left.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pooled investment whose shares pass to surviving subscribers until the last survivor takes all.

clue.text: When limited reflection may leave one in the dark

definitions.text: When limited reflection may leave one in the dark

parts.words: When limited reflection may leave one in the dark
parts.note: read literally: at this lunar phase the satellite reflects almost no sunlight towards us, so nights are dark

explanation.surface: A remark about how too little thinking leaves a person ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' and 'in the dark' look like thought and ignorance, but they are literal: sunlight bounced off the moon and a moonless night.
explanation.definitionFit: At this phase of the lunar cycle the moon's lit side faces away, reflecting almost no light to Earth.

clue.text: Heavenly body appears and a fellow is producing poem

parts.note: Venus is a planet, a heavenly body
taken as written
a don is a fellow of a university college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celestial object and a man together turn out a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is a university lecturer, often a college fellow at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's narrative poem of 1593 tells of the goddess's love for a beautiful youth.

clue.text: A newcomer for a term

parts.note: read 'term' as a word: a recently coined word is a new arrival in the vocabulary, not a pupil starting school for one term

explanation.surface: A new pupil arrives for one school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newcomer' and 'term' suggest a new pupil in school; the real sense is a newly coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a newly invented word or expression, a fresh coinage in the language.

clue.text: Discovers pendulum is showing failure to balance

indicators.note: showing means on display within the clue's words, so the answer is found inside them

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pendulum that refuses to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests a swinging pendulum at rest; the definition is about budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more than budgeted means the accounts fail to balance.

clue.text: Like delicate china controversially broken in Lilliput

definitions.meaning: a very thin, fragile porcelain is named for its likeness to this
in Gulliver's Travels the Lilliputians fight a war over which end of a boiled egg should be cracked

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain gets smashed amid a row in a tiny land.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift's satire has Big-Endians and Little-Endians at war over which end to break an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the thin brittle egg covering: the fine china is named after it, and in Swift it is what gets cracked.

clue.text: Getting it into perspective, fat's primarily for energy

indicators.note: primarily here means in first place, so the other pieces stand in front of the fat

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy
shortening is fat used in baking pastry

explanation.surface: A dietary note that fat is chiefly a source of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' says the short pieces come first. Shortening is a baking fat, mainly an American term. 'Getting it into perspective' is meant literally, as in drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: In drawing, depicting an object as shorter to show depth is rendering it in perspective.

clue.text: Ironic title man may want to write

definitions.meaning: a mock-respectful way of referring to a self-important man
a man might need his own pen points to write

explanation.surface: A man wants to write under a mocking title.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey honorific; the second reads the phrase literally, the pen nibs belonging to him.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mock title for a self-important man, and literally means the pen points belonging to him.

clue.text: Income derived from flat in Continental way

indicators.note: in places the flat piece inside the Continental way

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way on the Continent
even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Someone earns money from renting out a flat on a European street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially of a state or business.

clue.text: One sells food sounding comparatively unrefined

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for the phrase beside it is said aloud

parts.note: grosser is the comparative of gross, coarse or unrefined

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who sounds rather coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household goods.

clue.text: After surgery hours, doctor pops in lozenge

indicators.note: pops in means slips inside, so the doctor goes into the rearranged letters
after an operation something is rearranged, so the letters of the next word are reworked

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Once the clinic closes, the GP drops by with a throat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After surgery' looks like time, but it signals an anagram, giving RHOUS. 'lozenge' looks like a cough sweet but is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a diamond shape, an equilateral parallelogram with oblique angles.

clue.text: Powerful insect with flimsy wings

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: wings are the extremities, so take the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A strong insect with fragile wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' looks like the insect's wings but picks the first and last letters of 'flimsy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means muscular and strong, so powerful.

clue.text: Opposite to area with bombs on both sides

parts.note: V1s were German flying bombs of the Second World War, written VIS
the same flying bombs again, the second copy for the other side

explanation.surface: A war report: facing an area flanked by bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on both sides' sets one copy of the bombs before A and one after it. V1s were the 'doodlebug' flying bombs fired at London.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means face to face, used as a preposition for facing or in relation to.

clue.text: Very fit — or not in good shape?

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being very fit means being out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy but is a bout of fever. 'not in good shape' means shapeless, ill-defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague lacks clear outline or definite form.

clue.text: Separate runs covered by notice I edited in Standard

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside, so the runs go within the reworked letters
separate says the two runs go in apart, at different places in the reworked letters
edited means revised and rearranged, so the letters of notice and I are reworked

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the same runs abbreviation again, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor separates the scores in a notice for a paper called the Standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' turns NOTICE I into CITEION; 'covered by' and 'Separate' put one R after the C and another after the E. 'Standard' looks like the London newspaper but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a benchmark or principle by which things are judged, a standard.

clue.text: Old comic's enviable achievement, going round clubbing

definitions.meaning: a British boys' comic paper of 1950-69, home of Dan Dare
in golf, a hole played two strokes under par is a prized feat on a round

explanation.surface: An ageing comedian boasts of a feat while doing the rounds of the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' suggests a comedian and 'clubbing' nightlife; the second is a golf round with clubs. The comic was a famous British weekly for boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the name of the bird of prey: the comic's title and the golf score two under par.

clue.text: In card game, lead's not in exposed hand on right

indicators.note: on in an across clue means attached after, so the trimmed hand follows the right
the lead is the first letter, and it is not in, so the opening letter drops out

parts.note: in bridge the dummy is the partner's hand laid face up on the table

explanation.surface: A bridge player reports that the opening card was missing from the hand laid face up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the bridge lead, but it means the first letter: DUMMY loses its D. In bridge the dummy's cards are exposed on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a card game where players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Period needed to contain wretched weed in flower

indicators.note: the period needed to contain something, so the next part goes inside it

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: wretched suggests something in a sorry, mangled state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener needs time to deal with a miserable weed in a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' gives EEDW. 'weed' looks like the definition beside 'flower', but it is the fodder; the flower is a small blue veronica.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a small blue-flowered plant, a common garden and wild flower.
